transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-18 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~49 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood Solutions), Samir Patel (NimbleThera CISO), Laura Cheng (Platform Ops), Diego Marquez (Cloud Eng), Ana Ruiz (Data Privacy)

Summary:
Light security intake focused on whether NimbleThera should use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem) given pharma data sensitivity and regulatory reqs. Main concerns: encryption & KMS ownership, audit logs and retention, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC & tenant isolation, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and data residency. Action items and POC kickoff discussed.

Topics Covered:
- SOC 2 / ISO documentation and evidence
- SSO / SAML and SCIM user provisioning
- RBAC and granular API key controls
- Audit logs, retention, and export to SIEM
- Encryption at rest/in transit + customer-managed KMS options
- Data retention, deletion guarantees, and egress policies
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, isolation)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i run the account here. quick round of intros?
[00:18] Samir Patel: Samir here, CISO at NimbleThera. i'll lead on compliance questions.
[00:26] Laura Cheng: Laura, platform ops. i'll be hands on with networking and infra.
[00:30] Diego Marquez: Diego, cloud engineer.
[00:32] Ana Ruiz: Ana, data privacy, i'll focus on retention and deletion.
[00:36] Maya Lin: Maya from Redwood, i'm the solutions engineer working on secure deployments.
[00:40] Ethan Cole: Ethan, solutions architect, i'll help map the POC.

[02:05] Jordan Hayes: great, high level NimbleThera use case — internal LLM assistant for clinical ops, some PII-like metadata, definitely regulated. can you summarize the must-haves from compliance?
[02:25] Samir Patel: sure. primary is SOC 2 Type II, then certain ISO27001 controls. we need SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning, RBAC so we can separate environments, full audit logging exported to our Splunk, and KMS where possible — ideally customer-managed keys. also retention: 7 years for certain audit trails, and we need ability to delete data on request.

[05:15] Maya Lin: okay thanks. quick note on Redwood capabilities: hosted API (fastest), dedicated pools with reserved GPUs for isolation, and private deployment (VPC package or on-prem). for KMS we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private, for hosted we offer envelope encryption with optional KMS bring-your-own for enterprise customers.

[06:30] Diego Marquez: can you unpack the KMS workflow? we want to avoid plaintext tokens hitting third-party services.
[06:40] Maya Lin: yeah. today we do TLS in transit always. at rest, for hosted, objects are encrypted with our service key; for enterprise agreements we can set up a customer-managed KMS where Redwood holds wrappers and the root key is in your KMS, so encrypted payloads remain opaque. Dedicated gives you direct KMS integration in your VPC and Private gives full control on-prem. small caveat: some telemetry for performance and billing remains metadata only.

[08:12] Samir Patel: telemetry -> we need to know what metadata you retain, specifically what identifiers are kept and for how long.
[08:25] Jordan Hayes: good question. default telemetry includes request timestamps, model variant, latency buckets, token counts; no PII by design. retention windows are configurable under enterprise contracts, typically 90 days for detailed traces, longer aggregated metrics. we'll provide an audit log export via S3 or forward to your Splunk.

[11:00] Ana Ruiz: about deletion — if a user asks for data deletion, how do you guarantee removal from backups and caches? this is critical for us.
[11:18] Maya Lin: deletion triggers an async purge flow. KV caches and prefix caches are configurable; for Dedicated/Private you can control cache TTLs and disable persistent application-level caching. back-ups are on a policy cycle; we can commit to a retention window and provide a documented process for scrubbing keys or applying crypto-erasures when required. we'll include the playbook in the SOC package.

[14:00] Laura Cheng: SSO — does Redwood support IdP-initiated SAML? and SCIM to provision service accounts?
[14:15] Ethan Cole: yes, we've done both. typical flow: SAML for SSO and RBAC mapping, SCIM for user/group provisioning. for Dedicated + Private we can run the SCIM endpoint behind your private network; for hosted we support SCIM over TLS to your SCIM-compatible IdP. mapping rules can be customized to apply roles (admin, dev, read-only).

[16:45] Samir Patel: audit logs — fields, format, and how we ingest to Splunk? we need immutable logs for certain controls.
[16:58] Maya Lin: logs include timestamp, actor (user/service key), route, model id, request id, tokens in/out counts, and operation outcome. we can stream logs to a customer S3 bucket or to your syslog/Splunk HEC endpoint. Logs are append-only in our system; for Dedicated we can hand over raw logs daily and for Private they never leave your VPC unless you opt-in.

[19:50] Diego Marquez: curious about network topology for Dedicated — do we expose a private endpoint? how does peering work?
[20:05] Ethan Cole: Dedicated runs in a reserved GPU fleet; we offer private endpoints or VPC peering depending on region. peering means traffic stays within cloud backbone and we don't traverse the public internet for model inference. there's a small NAT egress for management plane, but data plane can be configured VPC-only. we'll get you a diagram.

[22:30] Samir Patel: SOC 2 artifacts — can you share the actual report and scope? we need to validate controls mapping to our audit checklist.
[22:42] Jordan Hayes: yes, we will share the current SOC 2 Type II report and the scope doc. note: for some Hosted telemetry we may redact customer identifiers in the public SOC 2. for enterprise contracts we provide supporting evidence under NDA.

[25:15] Ana Ruiz: we have data residency needs in EU for some datasets. can you pin workloads to EU-only GPUs?
[25:30] Maya Lin: we support region routing and can pin models to EU regions. for Hosted customers we can route by policy; for Dedicated you can book capacity in target regions. Private on-prem remains the only option if you need complete physical control.

[28:05] Laura Cheng: RBAC, service keys — we need per-service-account scoping and ability to rotate keys centrally. how granular are the API keys?
[28:20] Maya Lin: API keys can be scoped per-project, per-model, and tied to rate/usage quotas. we support key rotation via the console or API. for enterprise we can integrate key lifecycle events with your secret manager via webhook.

[30:00] Diego Marquez: performance question — Dedicated vs Hosted, we expect high concurrent inference. how does batching and KV caches affect latency and cost?
[30:15] Ethan Cole: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and we can tune continuous batching to meet your latency SLOs. KV caches reduce token re-compute for repeated contexts — for private/dedicated you control cache sizing. Hosted uses adaptive batching but has slightly more variable latency. we can run benchmarks during the POC with your prompt set.

[33:40] Samir Patel: legal/procurement — any contractual clauses re data ownership / indemnity?
[33:55] Jordan Hayes: we assert customer retains ownership of their data; standard indemnities are negotiable on enterprise terms. we'll hand this to contracts; i can loop in legal once we agree on deployment model.

[36:10] Ana Ruiz: retention windows again — for audit logs we might need 7 years, for raw request bodies maybe 1 year. are custom retention policies possible?
[36:25] Maya Lin: yes, configurable retention per data class is available at enterprise tier. for Hosted we have defaults, but Dedicated/Private give you full control including long-term S3 archival.

[38:50] Laura Cheng: about SIEM integration — do you support field-level masking before sending logs? some fields may contain identifiers we don't want in third-party systems.
[39:05] Maya Lin: we support configurable log filters and redaction rules before export. for max security, with Private deployment you can keep all logs internal and configure exporters yourself.

[41:30] Samir Patel: what are common failure modes? if the primary region is down, do we fail open to a less-compliant region? that's a red flag for us.
[41:45] Ethan Cole: good point. routing policies are configurable — we can set failover to only compatible regions that meet your compliance boundaries. Redwood has automatic fallback policies but for enterprise deals we can lock the routing policy so failover doesn't cross restricted jurisdictions.

[44:00] Jordan Hayes: sounds like next steps: we'll share SOC2 + diagrams, Maya will draft TCO for Dedicated vs Private, and Ethan will plan a POC with Diego. any other blockers?
[44:18] Ana Ruiz: please include the erase/crypto-erase procedures in the SOC package.
[44:25] Jordan Hayes: noted.

[46:00] Laura Cheng: timeline-wise, we'll review SOC docs this week and aim to decide on pilot by next Tuesday.
[46:12] Jordan Hayes: perfect — i'll send notes and artifacts after the call. thanks everyone.
[47:00] Meeting end.
